description: Argus is an open-source monitoring tool for servers and applications, with an AI investigator built in. You run it on your own infrastructure with one Docker command, then add its SDK to your apps. It watches metrics, containers and processes, and when something looks wrong it investigates: it correlates metrics, logs and events and explains the likely root cause in plain language. Free and MIT licensed; your data never leaves your servers. The landing page should send people to the GitHub repo and the docs.

Free and MIT licensed; your data never leaves your servers. The landing page should send people to the GitHub repo and the docs.

Write the opening screen.

reply.question: Before the questions, here's what I took from your description.

statements.text: A dark background throughout, so it sits naturally beside terminals, logs and the tools your users already run.

calls.systemPrompt:
You write one question in a design interview inside Caret, a design tool. Caret runs the interview and decides the topics and their order. Your only job is the question about the heading typeface.

How it is shown: shown as type specimens. They can also search all of Google Fonts, or Skip.

Rules:
- Write for someone who builds software but has no design vocabulary. Short sentences. Say what a choice does and how it will look. A design term is fine only next to its plain meaning.
- Every option and its reason must come from what they told you about their product, in their words.
- Options must be real alternatives that look clearly different from each other.
- Put each option's numbers in its label where it has them (hex, px, ratio).
- Recommend exactly one option.
- Never offer anything on the Avoid line.

The heading typeface is used for page titles and section headings. Offer real Google Fonts families that suit this product. Each option's label is the family name exactly as Google Fonts spells it.

reply.question: Argus runs on people's own servers and sends them to GitHub and the docs. Which heading font fits that dark, open-source, technical feel?

options.label: Archivo

options.label: Outfit
options.reason: Round, geometric letters. Titles look modern and friendly rather than infrastructural — less like a tool you run yourself, more like a hosted startup product.

options.label: Zilla Slab
options.reason: A slab serif with open-source roots. Headings read like well-kept documentation, which suits a free, MIT-licensed project people self-host.

The decided foundation:
- surface (light or dark): Dark
- display-type (the heading typeface): IBM Plex Sans. Shown with the reason: Drawn for technical docs and code, so titles sit naturally next to terminal output and repo links. Plain, clear letter shapes stay sharp as white text on dark.
- body-type (the body typeface): Source Sans 3. Shown with the reason: Open, humanist sans with tall lowercase. Stays clear at 14 to 16px in setup steps and long docs, and pairs calmly next to IBM Plex Sans headings.
- type-scale (type size and weight): 16px body, headings ×1.2. Shown with the reason: Comfortable on a dark page. Headings stand apart without shouting, and the plain root cause text stays easy to read next to the GitHub and docs links.
- brand-color (the brand colour): #28a4f0
- secondary-color (a supporting colour): #8b7bf7. Shown with the reason: Filled in when you pressed Just finish it.
- accent-color (an accent colour): #2dd4bf. Shown with the reason: Filled in when you pressed Just finish it.
- neutral (the greys): Cool. Shown with the reason: Filled in when you pressed Just finish it.
- semantics (success/warning/error colours): #3fb950, #d29922, #f85149. Shown with the reason: Filled in when you pressed Just finish it.
- spacing (density and spacing): Tight, 4px base. Shown with the reason: Filled in when you pressed Just finish it.
- radius (corner rounding): Soft, 8px. Shown with the reason: Filled in when you pressed Just finish it.
- depth (shadows and depth): Subtle. Shown with the reason: Filled in when you pressed Just finish it.

reply.summary: Your foundation is built for a dark monitoring product where people read root-cause text next to logs and repo links, so the type stays plain and comfortable and the page stays calm. IBM Plex Sans headings and Source Sans 3 body text share the same technical, no-frills feel, and the tight spacing and 8px corners keep everything dense and precise like a dashboard. The colour set gives you one lead colour to point at GitHub and the docs, with two supporting colours for charts and states.
reply.rule: The brand colour #28a4f0 carries every action and link, so GitHub and docs buttons always look the same; #8b7bf7 and #2dd4bf only ever appear as supporting marks such as chart lines or small highlights, never on buttons or text you need to read.

reasons.surface: Dark keeps the page easy on the eyes for people who stare at terminals all day, and makes the bright status colours #3fb950, #d29922 and #f85149 stand out instantly.
reasons.display-type: IBM Plex Sans was drawn for technical material, so headings sit naturally next to terminal output and repo links and stay sharp as white text on dark.
reasons.body-type: Source Sans 3 has tall lowercase letters that stay clear at 14 to 16px, so setup steps and long docs read without strain.
reasons.type-scale: 16px body with headings at ×1.2 keeps the plain root-cause text comfortable on dark while headings separate clearly without shouting.
reasons.brand-color: #28a4f0 marks every clickable thing, so a visitor always knows where the GitHub and docs links are on the page.
reasons.secondary-color: #8b7bf7 gives a quieter second colour for chart lines and supporting marks, so the brand colour stays the only thing that looks like a button.
reasons.accent-color: #2dd4bf adds a third note for small highlights and the AI investigator moment, keeping the page from looking one-note.
reasons.neutral: Cool greys match the technical, screen-lit feel of a monitoring tool and let the brighter colours do the pointing.
reasons.semantics: #3fb950, #d29922 and #f85149 give healthy, warning and failure states the same meaning they already have inside Argus, so the page and the tool agree.
reasons.spacing: A tight 4px base packs more onto screen, which suits a dashboard audience and lets steps and lists read like a tool, not a brochure.
reasons.radius: Soft 8px corners keep buttons and cards from feeling harsh while still reading as sharp and precise.
reasons.depth: Subtle shadows lift cards slightly off the dark background without adding glow or weight that would fight the text.
